feed.title: Biomedical AI Lab
feed.subtitle: We use machine learning to advance medicine, from wearable sensing and clinical gait analysis to language and imaging models for health.

entry.title: Our new website
entry.content: The Biomedical AI Lab has a new website. It brings our research themes, publications, people, apps and teaching together in one place, and our publication list now updates itself from DOIs and ORCID.

entry.title: Best poster at the Shriners Children’s State of the Science meeting

link.title: Best poster at the Shriners Children’s State of the Science meeting

entry.content: Our poster on SHAPE-UP, an AI approach to assessing arm function in children with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, won the best poster award out of 19 posters at the 2026 Shriners Children’s Annual State of the Science Meeting: AI and Orthopaedics in Atlanta. Lab members also presented work on long-term outcomes after pediatric-onset spinal cord injury, fall-risk assessment with instruction-tuned language models, and attention-based updates to the Shriners Gait Index.

entry.title: NIH funds a summer research program in digital health

link.title: NIH funds a summer research program in digital health

entry.content: A new NIH R25 award, with Prof. Albert as Co-PI, funds Advancing Digital Health Technology, a summer research program for high school and community college educators, from 2025 to 2030.

entry.title: Prof. Albert named Chair of Information Science

link.title: Prof. Albert named Chair of Information Science

entry.content: Prof. Mark V. Albert became Chair of the Department of Information Science in September 2025. He continues to direct the Biomedical AI Lab and remains an Associate Professor of Computer Science and Engineering with a joint appointment in Biomedical Engineering.
